one_month_reasoning: The one scheduled event in the window is Q3 2026 earnings on Oct 21, 2026 after the close (Nasdaq/Zacks; consensus Q3 EPS $2.39, about the midpoint of TI's $2.23-2.57 guide). Supply-chain trackers (Fusion Worldwide Greensheet, Sep 24; GlobX price-increase log) show TI enforcing new pricing on open POs and lead times still lengthening, so a Q3 beat and a Q4 guide above the $2.18 consensus look more likely than not. But in July a beat-and-raise produced a ~19% sell-the-news drawdown, and the stock has just bounced about 12% from mid-September levels, including +8% on the Oct 2 sector rally. So I expect good numbers with a reaction of uncertain sign. I keep the distribution almost symmetric around spot, with the median at about $295 (dividend aside, slight positive drift for the likely beat) and a 1-month sigma of about 12.5% (42%/3.5 = 12% plus an earnings-day premium). There are no other stock-specific events in the window; macro prints (CPI, payrolls) are second-order.

fair_value.method: 60% P/E: 2028 EPS of $12.00 (consensus $11.59 plus 3.5% for pricing) x 24x, the peer median of calendar-2027 P/E, gives $288. 40% FCF yield: 2028 FCF/share of about $11.30 at a 3.75% yield gives $301. The blend is about $293, roughly today's price.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: CY2028 EPS $12.00 x 24.0x (12-month-forward valuation rolls to CY2028 earnings)

inputs_detail.derivation: Nasdaq/Zacks annual forecast table; Yahoo shows CY26 $8.51 and CY27 $10.10, a similar path.

Consensus $11.59 + ~3.5%. Distributor/broker trackers show TI price increases (up to 85% on select parts in April 2026) and new pricing enforced on open POs as of Sep 2026. This pricing is not fully in sell-side numbers yet: CY27 consensus implies only ~14% revenue growth (Yahoo $24.9B vs $21.9B).

Median calendar-2027 P/E of 10 analog/MCU/power peers is 24.2x (range 14.6x-74.9x). The large-cap analog core (ADI, MCHP, NXPI, ON, STM) has a median of 20.7x, and ADI, the closest comp, is 25.0x. I use the peer median with no premium: TXN's ROIC and margins are higher, but its CY27 EPS growth (+16%) is below the peer median and its multiple is cyclically elevated.

EPS $12.00 + D&A ~$2.50/share, then minus capex ~$2.80/share and working capital ~$0.40/share. D&A ≈ TTM EBITDA $9.52B less TTM operating income (~38% x $19.45B ≈ $7.4B) ≈ $2.1B, rising with the Sherman ramp. Capex uses the $2-3B 2026 guide midpoint over ~905M shares.

TXN's TTM FCF yield is ~2.0% ($5.36B / $268B), depressed by the end of the capex wave. A mid-cycle 3.5-4% (about 25-28x FCF) matches the ~24-26x peer-median earnings and EBITDA multiples, given FCF ≈ net income once capex normalises.

bear.story: The 2027 analog shortage turns into double-ordering, as the 60-70 week lead times and price hikes on open POs did in 2021-22. Inventory correction signals appear by mid-2027, CY28 EPS is cut to ~$9.5 and the multiple derates to ~21x, giving ~$200.

base.story: The upcycle runs through 2027 and EPS tracks slightly above consensus ($10+ CY27, ~$12 CY28) on pricing and data-center/industrial strength. The multiple compresses from ~30x CY27 toward the ~24x peer median on CY28 EPS, so the price holds near $300 plus a ~2% dividend.

bull.story: Pricing power and Sherman 300mm cost advantage push margins toward the prior peak (~50% operating) and CY28 EPS reaches ~$14. The market pays ~28x for a multi-year capex-free FCF ramp, giving ~$400.

comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: TXN trades at 29.9x CY2027 consensus EPS ($9.84) and ~25x estimated forward EBITDA, above the 24.2x peer P/E median and well above the 20.7x large-cap analog core. My valuation applies 24.0x to CY2028 EPS, which is at the peer median and inside the range.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium is applied. TXN's structural advantages are real: 25.5% ROIC, ~42% operating margin in Q2 2026, 300mm internal capacity and the end of its capex wave. But its consensus CY27 EPS growth (+16%) is below the peer median, and the current multiple reflects early-upcycle optimism that has historically mean-reverted at the cycle peak. I could not show from the evidence that a premium would last through the horizon, so I use the peer median.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$215 (-27%) the market would be pricing ~$9 of CY28 EPS at ~24x or a sub-20x trough multiple. That most likely means the shortage/price-hike phase has flipped into a destocking cycle (lead times shortening, distributor inventory up, Q4/Q1 guides below seasonal) rather than ordinary 42%-vol noise. It also sits near the bear case and the analyst-target low ($225).

key_uncertainties: Whether the 2026 shortage (60-70 week precision-analog lead times, TI price hikes enforced on open POs) is real end demand or double-ordering that reverses in 2027 as in 2022.
Durability of TI pricing gains and the margin flow-through as Sherman SM1/SM2 utilisation ramps.
Multiple compression: TXN at ~30x CY27 EPS vs a 24x peer median; a rerating to the large-cap analog core (~21x) is worth ~-15%.
Macro/industrial cycle: a Kalshi 2026 recession contract traded ~26% (tracker, volume not shown).
China competition in mature-node analog and tariff policy.
reasoning: Basic facts: Q2 2026 revenue $5.46B (+23% y/y), EPS $2.17, operating margin 42%, Q3 guide $5.65-6.15B / $2.23-2.57 (TIKR recap), net debt $7.05B, 913M shares. Consensus EPS is $8.45 (CY26), $9.84 (CY27), $11.59 (CY28) per Nasdaq/Zacks; Yahoo has $10.10 for CY27. My lane's main finding comes from distributor and broker trackers (Fusion Worldwide Greensheet, Sep 24 2026; GlobX price-increase log; TrustCompo). Analog is in a genuine shortage: TI enforces new prices on open POs, TPS/SN74 lead times keep stretching, TMCS parts draw 300% premiums, and ADI precision parts are at 60-70 weeks. That points to upside to near-term estimates (I add ~3.5% to CY28 EPS). It is also the classic late-upcycle signature that preceded the 2022 analog derating, so it fattens the left tail 12 months out. Independent newsletters (TIKR) document the July sell-the-news drop from $334 to ~$254-262 despite rising targets, so the stock is already valuing strong numbers. I value on one consistent calendar-2027 consensus basis for 10 peers (median 24.2x; ADI 25.0x; large-cap analog core 20.7x). TXN at 29.9x CY27 earns no premium beyond the peer median, since its EPS growth is lower and ROIC/margin advantages are cyclically flattered. That gives a fair value of ~$293 (P/E $288, FCF yield $301), about spot. Scenarios are $200/25%, $300/50% and $400/25%, a mean of ~$300. The ladder is a lognormal with median ~$295 and sigma ~0.38 (slightly below the 42% realized vol, as an early-cycle mega-cap), with the left tail fattened for a cycle turn (P(≥$206) 0.79 vs 0.83 lognormal). Limits: X/Twitter and Reddit were not directly fetchable and searches surfaced no Reddit threads, so social sentiment comes from newsletters. Forward EV/EBITDA for peers is my own scaling of TTM EBITDA, not consensus EBITDA. The Kalshi recession quote comes from a third-party tracker without volume. Independent long-horizon newsletter models (TIKR: ~$514-524 by 2030, about 10-14% IRR) imply a mid-teens-percent annual return from spot. That fits a 12-month median near today's price plus dividend, not a large re-rating.
